uncited: - **Scale Space Grid $L$**: 3D array of floats, same dimensions as input volume. $L(x; t)$ stores the diffused intensity at position $x$ and scale $t$.
Compute the normalized Laplacian $N(x) = t \cdot \nabla^2 L(x; t)$ for all voxels.
Identify voxels $x$ that are local maxima in the 3D spatial neighborhood (e.g., 26-connected) at scale $t$.
Check if the scale $t$ is a local maximum along the scale axis (compare with $t-\Delta t$ and $t+\Delta t$).
If both conditions are met, add $(x, t)$ to the Scale Abstraction $\mathcal{N}$.
- For a sample point $x$ and a LoG extremum $x_i$, cast a ray from $x_i$ to $x$.
- If any voxel along the ray has a scalar value or gradient magnitude below threshold $\tau$, the point $x$ is not "visible" from $x_i$.
- **Time Complexity**: Scale-space computation is $O(n \cdot V \cdot |\mathcal{N}|)$ where $V$ is number of voxels and $|\mathcal{N}|$ is stencil size.
Backprojection is $O(V \cdot |\mathcal{N}_{abstraction}|)$, which can be expensive if many extrema are detected.
- **Memory Complexity**: Requires storing the scale space $L$ for all iterations if backprojection is done offline, or just the current layer if streaming.
The abstraction list size depends on feature complexity.
